A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SeqAfford and are readable, including their figures, tables and equations. v1 ends after the references; v2 retains the main paper and adds supplementary Sections A-G. The supplied material supports a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original affordance-segmentation evaluations in Table 2, component and backbone ablations in Tables 3-4, and qualitative predictions in Figure 5.

after.justification: v2 retains these experimental results and adds dataset analyses and qualitative predictions and comparisons in the supplement.

M1.justification: v1 Figure 4 assigns Hseg to Q and dense point features to K,V; v2 reverses these assignments. However, Section 4.2 retains the original assignment. This conflict prevents determining whether the attention procedure changed or the diagram is erroneous. Appendix E otherwise documents existing components in greater detail.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same 23-category dataset and single/sequential affordance tasks, including seen/unseen and multi-object settings. The supplement supplies additional examples within this existing coverage without establishing a new dataset, domain or task.

E2.justification: Table 2 retains the same quantitative comparators. Figure A12 newly includes LASO in a side-by-side qualitative comparison, whereas v1's qualitative figures show only SeqAfford. LASO corresponds to the existing PointRefer [12] comparator; its participation in qualitative comparison is the limited addition.

E3.justification: The reported model configuration, training budget, evaluation metrics and sequential-baseline procedure remain unchanged. Table A1 newly discloses training/test split counts for existing experiments; it does not establish that those splits changed.

E4.justification: Figures A7-A8 add dataset characterization through question-length distributions and word clouds. Figures A10-A12 add single/sequential case studies and two qualitative LASO comparisons. The component and backbone ablations in Tables 3-4 remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, performance uncertainty intervals or significance tests. The added dataset counts and distributions do not introduce uncertainty estimation for experimental performance.

E6.justification: Tables 2-4 retain their numerical results and rankings, including SeqAfford's Table 2 mIoU values of 19.5, 13.8 and 14.6 for seen, unseen and sequential settings. v2 adds question-length counts and qualitative predictions and comparisons in Figures A7 and A10-A12.

T1.justification: Appendix E.1 adds Equations 5-10 explicitly defining sampled point sets and feature-propagation/upsampling dependencies, including H8 and H4 feature inputs. These extend the mathematical specification beyond v1's high-level description. No theorem, proof or theoretical guarantee is added.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same scientific contributions: sequential 3D affordance reasoning, the approximately 180K-pair benchmark, and SeqAfford's multimodal reasoning and segmentation capabilities. The added evidence does not redefine these claims.

C2.justification: Appendix E.2 newly explains and justifies deriving affordance order from generated object nouns, relying on the language model producing the correct textual sequence. The broader world-knowledge interpretation and scene-level future-work discussion remain unchanged.

D1.justification: The supplement substantially expands reproducibility information through generation prompts, question/answer templates, dataset split counts, feature-propagation details and multi-object output handling. The abstract also adds a code/data access link, although Appendix A inconsistently says release will follow acceptance.

R1.justification: The same 43 cited works and substantive research positioning are retained. The supplement reuses existing references, including LASO, PointNet++, DGCNN and Uni3D; changed citation back-references do not add related work.

P1.justification: The main narrative and section order remain almost verbatim. v2 adds an availability sentence and an organized supplement with a contents list and expanded explanations, without extensively rewriting or reorganizing the existing argument.

P2.justification: The supplement adds Table A1 and Figures A1-A12, substantially expanding the visual explanation of prompts, dataset characteristics, implementation and predictions. Figure 4 is relabeled and moved from page 7 to page 6, while Table 2 moves to page 7.

improvement.justification: v2 improves inspectability and reproducibility by supplying previously absent prompt formats, split counts and implementation details, alongside additional qualitative comparisons. The overall gain is limited because quantitative validation is unchanged, Figure 4 now conflicts with the attention description, and code/data release statements are inconsistent. The documentation benefits support a modest improvement despite these defects.
